title: Of Course
novel:
Robin began dating a man named Don. She tried to act [[casual|casual]], but her smile betrayed her. She was [[genuinely|genuine]] happy for the first time in months.

Barney, however, could not let it go. He was too [[competitive|competitive]] and too [[jealous|jealous]] to quit. He [[schemed|scheme]] to break them up, [[recruiting|recruit]] old flames and inventing lies. Each plan [[collapsed|collapse]].

Robin discovered the plots and [[confronted|confront]] Barney. "Why can't you let me be happy?" she asked.

Barney could not [[confess|confess]] the truth. The real reason — that he still cared — was too [[fragile|fragile]] to say out loud.

To [[deflect|deflect]] attention, Robin wrote a silly song about Canada and performed it at the bar. The gang laughed until they cried. Even Don, watching from a corner, had to admit she was [[charming|charm]].

Barney watched with [[regret|regret]], but said nothing. Some [[admissions|admission]], Ted sighed, stayed [[unspoken|unspoken]] not because they were false, but because they were too true.

jealous.en: angry that someone you like is with another

recruit.en: to find people to join a plan

confront.en: to face someone and challenge them

deflect.en: to turn attention away from something

regret.en: a sad feeling about something you did
